title: Job graph panel: show the setups of a job and the order of their operations as a graph, in a bottom panel

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
The maintainer asked for this issue on 2026-11-15 and set its priority to `P?` (paused):

> Second issue is the final output of it should be the "setup" of a job, and its ordering visualized on a graph rather than thru the browser tree.. its a nice visual addition. Put both as P?

About the panel he said: "as a hidden panel not open by default that snaps to the bottom of the viewpoert when opened.. so its not that high but full width."

Depends on: #1956 (the node graph crate).

What is wanted:
- A panel that is hidden by default. A menu entry and a shortcut open it.
- When open, it docks at the bottom of the viewport, at full width and with a small height. The user can change the height.
- The graph shows the job: each setup, the operations of each setup in their machining order, and the tool of each operation.
- A click on a node selects that entity through the `SelectEntity` command, as the browser tree does. The selection in the tree and in the graph is the same.
- The browser tree stays. The graph is an added view.

Step 1 is read-only. Later steps (each one its own issue, when this one is released from `P?`):
- Drag a node to change the order of the operations, or to move an operation to a different setup. Each such edit is an undoable command and gets its MCP tool.

Rules that apply:
- The panel does not read the ECS world directly. The app layer gives it a plain graph snapshot (AGENTS.md "Dependencies").
- Node positions come from the automatic layout. The project file does not store them in step 1, thus the file version does not change.
- The structural tests assert the panel: hidden by default, its label, its dock position, one node for each setup and operation. No pixel snapshot is added in the PR.
- The PR has before and after screenshots in its body.

Done means: the panel opens at the bottom of the viewport, shows the setups and the operation order of the open job, and a click on a node selects the entity.
